originalFindings.title: Unresolved Water Damage Source and Scope Definition
originalFindings.observation: The source of the water damage in Room B104 remains unconfirmed despite initial removal of 18 m² of flooring, creating an unknown risk for the repair scope.
originalFindings.consequence: Uncertainty regarding the water source may lead to incomplete remediation or future structural issues if the root cause is not addressed before finalizing the repair.
originalFindings.action: Investigate and confirm the specific source of the water damage to validate the repair scope and prevent recurrence.
originalFindings.uncertainty: Cause of damage is unknown; scope relies on visual observation of removal only.

evidence.quote: Water damage was observed near the east wall. The source has not been confirmed. No standing water remained at the start of the shift.
Removed approximately 18 m2 of flooring in Room B104. Debris placed in designated container. Exposed substrate photographed.
The report says the area is ready for base preparation, but does not record a substrate inspection, acceptance, or sign-off.
Crew was told verbally at 07:20 that the area was cleared to proceed. No written release or inspection record was available at the workface.
No inspector name, inspection time, checklist, or written acceptance is referenced. The subcontractor's report for the same day states that written release was still outstanding at 15:30.

At 10:15, foreman checked with the GC. Written inspection release had not been received. RFI-017 asks whether the replacement slab should match the original thickness or revised detail; no response was available to the crew.

originalFindings.title: Missing Formal Substrate Inspection Acceptance
originalFindings.observation: Initial reports indicated a missing substrate inspection and acceptance, but a later report (DR-A07) confirms a signed inspection (QC-B104-0514) was completed and accepted.
originalFindings.consequence: The delay in placing concrete was caused by the lack of a formal written release, not the absence of the inspection itself, which was subsequently performed.
originalFindings.action: None required for the inspection status; ensure the signed checklist QC-B104-0514 is archived and linked to the project records.
originalFindings.uncertainty: Historical reports (DR-A02 through DR-A05) claimed the inspection was missing or pending, but DR-A07 explicitly states it was completed and signed.

evidence.quote: The report says the area is ready for base preparation, but does not record a substrate inspection, acceptance, or sign-off.

No inspector name, inspection time, checklist, or written acceptance is referenced. The subcontractor's report for the same day states that written release was still outstanding at 15:30.

At 10:15, foreman checked with the GC. Written inspection release had not been received. RFI-017 asks whether the replacement slab should match the original thickness or revised detail; no response was available to the crew.
Inspection completed at 08:10. Substrate accepted for placement subject to using the approved slab detail and documenting reinforcement placement. Signed checklist recorded as QC-B104-0514.
Signed checklist QC-B104-0514 referenced

originalFindings.title: Unresolved RFI-017 Regarding Slab Thickness
originalFindings.observation: RFI-017 asking whether the replacement slab should match the original thickness or a revised detail remains open throughout the sequence, despite internal notes suggesting a decision.
originalFindings.consequence: The concrete crew could not proceed with the pour until the design team formally issued a response, causing a multi-day delay in the critical path.
originalFindings.action: Design Team to issue a formal RFI response identifying the specific drawing revision or confirming the original detail.
originalFindings.uncertainty: Internal engineering notes (DR-A06) suggested a decision ('use original detail') but lacked formal transmission or attachment.

evidence.quote: At 10:15, foreman checked with the GC. Written inspection release had not been received. RFI-017 asks whether the replacement slab should match the original thickness or revised detail; no response was available to the crew.
RFI-017 reviewed internally. Engineer's note says 'use original detail' but the response was not transmitted through the formal RFI system.
The signed checklist confirms substrate acceptance, but does not resolve the slab thickness question in RFI-017.
Crew received a message from the GC saying 'detail should be the same as before.' The message did not identify a drawing number or revision, and RFI-017 still appeared open in the system.
Report states the pour used the approved detail, but does not cite the drawing revision or attach the formal RFI-017 response. Reinforcement inspection reference is listed as RI-B104-0515.

originalFindings.title: Unverified Reinforcement Inspection and Detail Confirmation
originalFindings.observation: Reinforcement inspection was requested but not completed in early reports; later reports indicate reinforcement was placed and a specific inspection record (RI-B104-0515) was cited after the pour.
originalFindings.consequence: Concrete placement proceeded based on a verbal instruction ('detail should be the same as before') rather than a formal drawing revision or completed inspection, introducing a coordination risk.
originalFindings.action: Verify that the placed reinforcement matches the final approved detail (original or revised) and ensure record RI-B104-0515 is attached to the project file.
originalFindings.owner: General Contractor / Design Team / Quality Inspector
originalFindings.uncertainty: Early reports (DR-A08) stated reinforcement inspection was not yet completed, but DR-A09 cites a specific inspection record after the pour.

evidence.quote: Crew received a message from the GC saying 'detail should be the same as before.' The message did not identify a drawing number or revision, and RFI-017 still appeared open in the system.
Confirm approved drawing revision and complete reinforcement inspection before placement.
Report states the pour used the approved detail, but does not cite the drawing revision or attach the formal RFI-017 response. Reinforcement inspection reference is listed as RI-B104-0515.
Delivery tickets referenced; RFI response not attached

originalFindings.title: Unquantified Concrete Placement and Missing Formal RFI Response
originalFindings.observation: Concrete was placed (4.2 m³ delivered) after the RFI-017 was listed as 'resolved' by the superintendent, but the formal response document was never attached to the report.
originalFindings.consequence: The project record lacks proof that the poured concrete matches the approved design detail due to the missing formal RFI response attachment.
originalFindings.action: Attach the formal RFI-017 response and the reinforcement inspection record to the project closeout documentation.
originalFindings.uncertainty: Superintendent noted RFI-017 as resolved, but the report itself does not contain the formal response or drawing revision.

originalFindings.observation: Electrical crew experienced a temporary access restriction (3 hours 45 minutes) due to concrete activities, but the report does not identify who issued the restriction or provide advance notice.
originalFindings.consequence: The electrical subcontractor incurred an unplanned delay without prior coordination, potentially affecting their schedule and creating a claim risk.
originalFindings.action: GC to confirm the notification procedure for adjacent trades and document any verified schedule impact for the electrical subcontractor.
originalFindings.uncertainty: Report states work was restricted but does not specify the issuer or the timing of the notice relative to the electrical crew's arrival.
